clause.quote: When an exchange message is not part of a transaction, the Exchange Identifier, `x` field value, MUST be the empty string.

inferred_from.inference: The sentence binds the sender. An exchange message whose `x` names no exchange inception the validator holds is refused under either reading of whether it belongs to a transaction: outside one, this sentence requires `x` to be empty; inside one, the transaction's first message must be an `xip` ("The first message MUST be an Exchange Inception message with type `xip`."), and none with that SAID was delivered. Refusing it is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, IPEX).

description: A signed grant with an empty p and an x that names no exchange inception the validator holds, delivered alone. It is refused under either reading of whether it belongs to a transaction: outside one, x MUST be the empty string, and inside one the first message MUST be an xip, which was never delivered (KERI line 979). Both sentences bind the sender, so the refusal is an inferred SHOULD.

dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-09; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.
dispute.summary: KERI line 979 says x MUST be the empty string for an exchange message outside a transaction, and that a transaction's first message MUST be an xip, so a lone exn with a non-empty x is refused under either reading. Its generic exchange processing (Exchanger.processEvent in src/keri/peer/exchanging.py, with no route handler registered) reads neither p nor x, so it accepts a signed exn whatever its transaction link says. keripy's own IPEX starts exchanges this way, with an x that is the digest of a fresh nonce and no xip (apply, offer and grant in src/keri/acdc/ipexing.py). The refusal is an inferred SHOULD, since the sentences bind the sender.

title: A lone exchange message with an empty prior and a non-empty exchange id
